discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (moire materials, flat-band superconductivity)
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011) predicted that at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees the Dirac bands of bilayer graphene become nearly flat, making kinetic energy negligible relative to interactions. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group realised this with precise tear-and-stack fabrication, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in a single tunable material. This opened the field of twistronics: moire systems now host orbital ferromagnetism, quantum anomalous Hall states, fractional Chern insulators without magnetic field, and superconductivity across graphene multilayers and transition-metal dichalcogenides, confirmed by many laboratories worldwide. The discovery also revealed that superfluidity in flat bands is governed by band quantum geometry, linking topology and superconductivity in a fundamentally new way. A clear theoretical prediction followed by an ingenious experimental realisation, it created a versatile platform for strongly correlated quantum matter.
